passage:
Last weekend, my father took me to his old study. On the shelf, there were 20 big books. They were the Children's Encyclopaedia he got when he was a boy.

An encyclopaedia is a book that tries to tell you about everything — animals, plants, planets, countries, famous people. Each article is short but clear. The books have an index at the end, so we can find any topic in a few seconds.

I opened Volume 5 and read about the moon. I learned that the moon is 384,000 kilometres from the Earth, and there is no air on it. Then I opened Volume 12 and learned about dinosaurs.

An encyclopaedia is like a small library. I can travel the world and visit the stars without leaving home. It is truly a treasure of knowledge.
q: How many big books were there on the shelf?
explain: 原文 “there were 20 big books”。

passage:
Numbers are everywhere. They tell the time, the price, the phone number and even the temperature.

The most common numbers are from zero to nine. With these ten digits we can write any number — from one to a billion and more. The Chinese people began to use the ten-digit system more than 3,000 years ago.

Different people like different numbers. In China, eight is a lucky number because it sounds like "getting rich". In the West, seven is lucky because there are seven days in a week and seven colours in a rainbow. But 13 is often seen as unlucky, so many buildings have no 13th floor.

Without numbers, there would be no math, no computers, no smartphones. Learn to love numbers — they make our life easier.
q: How many digits do we use to write any number?
explain: 原文 “the most common numbers are from zero to nine”，即十个数字。

passage:
I got my first computer last year for my thirteenth birthday. It was a small laptop, only 1.5 kilograms. I was so excited!

Dad showed me how to turn it on. The screen lit up and asked me to set a password. I chose one that I could remember. Then I learned how to use the mouse and keyboard.

On the first day, I typed a short letter to my grandma. It took me thirty minutes — I could only find one letter at a time! A week later, I could type much faster. I also learned to save my files in different folders: "homework", "music", "photos".

Now I use the computer every day. I write stories, watch English videos, and email my cousin in America. My world has become bigger. But I remember Dad's words: a computer is a tool — don't let it use you.
q: When did the writer get the first computer?
explain: 原文 “for my thirteenth birthday”。

passage:
Do you know the Four Great Inventions of ancient China? They are paper, the compass, printing and gunpowder. Each one changed the world.

Paper was invented in China about two thousand years ago. Before paper, people wrote on bamboo or silk. Bamboo was heavy and silk was expensive. Paper was light and cheap, so knowledge could travel far.

The compass was another great gift. It uses a magnetic needle that always points north. Sailors could now find their way on the open sea.

Printing made books cheap and common. Before printing, every book was copied by hand, and only rich people could buy them. After printing, more children could read.

Gunpowder was first used in medicine, then in fireworks, and later in warfare.

These four inventions flew from China to Europe along the Silk Road. They pushed the world into a new age.
q: What are the Four Great Inventions?
explain: 原文明确列出四大发明。

passage:
Have you ever learned a word in the morning and forgotten it by night? Don't worry — it happens to everyone. The good news is that memory is like a muscle. The more you train it, the stronger it grows.

Here are three simple tricks I use:

1) Repeat with space. I review a new word five minutes later, then one hour, one day, and one week. Each time the word goes deeper into my mind.

2) Make a picture. For the word "elephant", I imagine a pink elephant riding a bicycle. The crazier the picture, the harder it is to forget.

3) Tell a friend. When I explain a rule to my little brother, I understand it twice as well.

My English teacher says, "Your brain is not a warehouse, it is a garden. Water it every day, and the flowers will bloom."
q: What is memory compared to in the passage?
explain: 原文 “memory is like a muscle”。

passage:
Sun Wukong, also called the Monkey King, is one of the most loved heroes in Chinese stories. He was born from a stone on the Flower-Fruit Mountain. From the first day he was brave, clever and full of magic.

Sun Wukong learned 72 changes. He could turn himself into a tiger, a fish, or even a small fly. He also had a long gold stick that could grow as tall as the sky or shrink to the size of a needle.

In the famous story Journey to the West, Sun Wukong goes with the monk Tang Sanzang to bring Buddhist books back from India. The journey takes more than ten years. They meet eighty-one dangers on the way — demons, mountains of fire, and tricky spirits. But with courage and cleverness, Sun Wukong protects his master every time.

Why do children love Sun Wukong? Because he is not a perfect hero. He is naughty and proud, but he is also loyal and kind.
q: Where was Sun Wukong born?
options: From a stone on the Flower-Fruit Mountain
explain: 原文 “born from a stone on the Flower-Fruit Mountain”。

In the famous story Journey to the West, Sun Wukong goes with the monk Tang Sanzang to bring Buddhist books back from India. The journey takes more than ten years. They meet eighty-one dangers on the way — demons, mountains of fire, and tricky spirits. But with courage and cleverness, Sun Wukong protects his master every time.

Why do children love Sun Wukong? Because he is not a perfect hero. He is naughty and proud, but he is also loyal and kind.
q: Why do children love Sun Wukong?
options: Because he is a perfect hero
Because he is naughty but also loyal and kind
explain: 原文说他不完美却忠诚善良，故受喜爱。

passage:
China is a big country, and its weather is very different from north to south. Let's compare two cities — Harbin in the north and Guangzhou in the south.

In Harbin, winter lasts more than five months. From November to March, the temperature often falls below zero. The rivers freeze, and children skate on the ice. Every January, Harbin holds a famous Ice Festival. Huge buildings made of ice shine like crystal under the lights.

In Guangzhou, winter is short and mild. Even in January, we seldom see snow. People wear jackets, not heavy coats. But summer is hot and wet. From May to September, storms and typhoons come one after another. When a typhoon arrives, schools close and planes cannot fly.

Two cities, two worlds. But people in both places find joy.
q: How long does winter last in Harbin?
explain: 原文 “winter lasts more than five months”。

passage:
Last week was English Week at our school. Five wonderful days, full of English everywhere!

Monday — Opening ceremony. Our headmaster gave a short welcome speech in English. Every classroom door had a new name: Ocean Room, Star Room, Rainbow Room.

Tuesday — Reading day. Students brought their favourite English books to share. I showed my Harry Potter.

Wednesday — Speaking contest. Twenty students each gave a three-minute speech. I was number twelve. I was so nervous that my knees shook, but the audience clapped when I finished.

Thursday — Play night. Our class performed a short play of The Tortoise and the Hare. I played the tortoise.

Friday — Prize day. My speech won third prize! I took home a book and a shining medal.

English is not only a subject. It is a bridge that connects me to a bigger world.
q: How many days did English Week last?
explain: 原文 “Five wonderful days”。
